title: Maps [Keys]
description:
There is one more map method: Get. `get(key: <KeyType>): <ValueType>`. _Technically_, keys can be of any type. However. _**PLEASE DONT MAKE WEIRD KEYS**_.
```ts
const map = new Map<string[], string>();
map.set(["Hello,", " World!"], "Famous");
console.log(map.get(["Hello,", " World!"]));
// undefined
```
What? Why did that happen? See, arrays in TypeScript are _references_, not values. That means that means that `["me"] === ["me"]` is false. But that does mean that
```
const me: string[] = ["me"];
me === me // true
```
This means that you can create a variable that holds the key then using that as the key. PLEASE DONT DO THIS.

# Assignment:
MeTube uses private "Session Tokens" (objects) to securely look up live stream analytics. 
Create a function `getStreamStats` that takes a `sessionToken` object and a `statsMap` Map. It should return the string value associated with that **specific** token reference.
If a hacker creates a new object `{ id: "VIP" }` that looks exactly like a real token, the map should still return `undefined` because it isn't the same reference in memory!
